name: ASCENT: The Corponation Ladder Game
description: A brightly colored children's board game sold in Tier 3-4 toy shops, ostensibly a simple ladder-climbing race from Tier 1 to Tier 5, where players draw cards representing 'Opportunity Events' and 'Setback Events' as they ascend the track. The game's art is cheerful and the cards are written in encouraging corporate language, but the mathematical probability of ascending from Tier 1 to Tier 5 without a 'Debt Spiral' card is approximately 4%, a figure that has been independently verified by multiple statisticians. An AR overlay version for BCI-equipped children adds animated corponation mascots who cheer every setback as a 'learning moment.'
story_hooks: The original playtester notes for ASCENT have surfaced, showing that early versions had a 34% ascent probability — someone deliberately rebalanced the game to make climbing nearly impossible, and that person still works at Axiom.
A Tier 5 child playing the game draws a 'Debt Spiral' card and has a breakdown, prompting a Spire parenting crisis that briefly makes the game's statistics a matter of public record.

The pirated Shelf Edition has been modified further by an unknown party — this new version has a hidden win condition that triggers if all players collectively refuse to climb and instead redistribute their resources.
